result:
I saved the results to `answer.json`. I computed them with one script and ran it once, without checking the numbers a second way.

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| a. Segment with the highest Q3 net sales | `consumer`, 299,447,269원 |
| b. Customers with a paid order in Q3 | 247 |
| c. Category with the highest Q3 net sales | `sw`, 307,901,608원 |
| d. Month with the highest net sales (all periods) | 2025-07 |
| e. Customer with the largest Q3 refund total | `u161@ex.com` (3,357,100원) |
| f. Customers with 2 or more paid orders in Q3 | 233 |
| g. Average net sales per paid Q3 order | 675,035원 |
| h. Net sales growth, August → September 2025 | -9.4% |

For h, August was 290,256,850원 and September was 263,037,636원.

The data had a few quirks that affect the answers:
- **Segment names:** the same segment appears in different forms (`Enterprise `, ` consumer`, `SMB`). I trimmed the spaces and lowercased them so they group into three segments.
- **Shared emails:** the 300 customer accounts have only 250 distinct emails. For b, e and f, I counted accounts with the same email as one person.
- **Segment per order:** accounts that share an email can have different segments. For a, I used the segment of the account that placed each order.
- **Dates:** I added 9 hours to every timestamp to convert it to KST before assigning dates, months and quarters.

STATUS: DONE
